hero.caption: The outer corridor of the replica from 2000 of the Haltdalen Stave Church situated in the Vestmannaeyjar in Iceland (63.444301, -20.261203). (Paul Torvik Nilsen, 'Colourful Middle Ages', Tell'us: Science in Norway (December 2001), 6-9.)

images.caption: en:Haltdalen Stave Church (Haltdalen stavkyrkje), a small  stave church erected in the 1170s, rebuilt 1937 on Sverresborg Trøndelag Folk Museum, an open-air and cultural history museum with more than 60 buildings in the area surrounding "Sverresborg", the ruins of King Sverre's medieval castle (small fortress), in the city of Trondheim. Photo taken on a sunny spring day in April 2019.

images.caption: Haltdalen stave church at the Sverresborg Trøndelag Folk Museum in Trondheim, Norway, dates from the 1170s. The framework design common at the time features sold corner pillars called staves which frame upright planks called tiles.
